pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-N-Methyl-D-Aspartate Receptor (Anti-NMDAR) Encephalitis secondary to Ovarian Teratoma THE SMOKING GUN: A pelvic ultrasound revealing a mature ovarian teratoma (dermoid cyst), alongside the EEG finding of extreme delta brush and CSF positive for anti-GluN1 IgG antibodies. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Ectopic neural tissue expressed within the patient's ovarian teratoma breaches immune privilege, triggering the production of systemic antibodies against the GluN1 subunit of the NMDA receptor. These IgG antibodies cross the blood-brain barrier, binding to cell-surface NMDARs in the brain and causing receptor cross-linking and endocytosis. The resulting selective depletion of functional postsynaptic NMDARs disrupts GABAergic interneuron inhibition and frontostriatal signaling, yielding the progressive triad of psychosis, dyskinesias, and autonomic collapse.
